page: Google Cloud Platform e2-highcpu-16 is an x86_64 architecture virtual machine belonging to the E2 server family. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.2 GHz, supported by a cache configuration of 32 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate a mixed profile. The instance achieves strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and memory bandwidth tests fall within the average range. Tradeoffs are evident in single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, with gzip and bzip3 single-threaded benchmarks scoring in the bottom 10%, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rated as weak. Geekbench single-core and text processing scores also rank in the bottom 10%, while multi-core Geekbench tasks, software compilation, and ray tracing maintain average performance.

Given its 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the e2-highcpu-16 is designed for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The dedicated CPU allocation provides stable performance for multi-threaded processing, static web serving, and lightweight LLM inference on small models, where it maintains average throughput. The lack of bundled local storage and GPUs, combined with the lower memory density, makes this instance a cost-efficient option for parallelizable CPU tasks, software compilation, and basic image processing workloads that fit within the 16 GB memory limit.
